Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
801 PM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

.SYNOPSIS...27/112 PM.

A cooling trend will begin Saturday as the first in a series of
storms move through the region. The first chance for rain will be
Sunday afternoon, with off and on rain, very heavy at times, 
through at least Wednesday morning.

&&

.SHORT TERM (FRI-MON)...27/800 PM.

***UPDATE***

Another spectacular Srn CA day is in the books. 590 dam hgts and
offshore flow combined to bring the second consecutive day of
highs in the upper 70s to mid 80s (Woodland Hills hit 90) which
were 8 to 12 degrees above normal.

A broad shield of high clouds moving ahead of a strong storm will
bring an end to the sunny skies tomorrow. These clouds and a 
switch to onshore flow in the afternoon will bring 3 to 6 degrees 
of cooling to most areas. Despite this cooling max temps will end 
up 4 to 8 degrees above normal.

All eyes remain on the Tuesday storm with a quick look at the 00Z
mdls showing not much change to the current storm forecast.

Current forecast is in good shape and no updates are needed.

***From Previous Discussion***

Coast and coastal valley temperatures will drop off sharply this 
weekend as onshore flow returns and the massive ridge gets pushed 
to the east by the next storm system. Most of those areas will 
cool off by 4-8 degrees each of the next two days, bringing highs 
back down to normal or even a little below normal by Sunday and 
Monday. Interior areas, as usual after a Santa Ana, will either 
warm slightly or remain about the same this weekend then cool 
Monday as next system moves in.

Speaking of which, the first in a series of storms will be moving
into the Central Coast as early as Sunday afternoon with some 
light scattered showers. Those will make their way south Sunday
night into Monday morning. Amounts in most areas through Monday
afternoon are expected to be under a quarter inch, except as much
as a half inch along the Central Coast.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...27/237 PM.

No big changes in the forecast for the primary storm next week,
which now seems to begin as early as Monday night. Models are in
very good agreement showing the upper low crossing 140w close to
36 degrees north latitude which is much farther south than usual
and sets up a track towards southern California that is
climatologically favored to produce severe weather, especially in
LA County. This track will also cross over SSTs that are still
5-10 degrees above normal. So it's not surprising that many of the
ensemble solutions increased rain amounts, particularly on 
Tuesday when there is at least a 20-30 percent chance of rain 
rates reaching or exceeding 1 inch per hour in the upslope areas 
south of Point Conception. 

As we've been emphasizing, residents, especially in areas that 
are compromised by fires in the last year or two should pay close 
attention to the forecasts and begin preparations to protect your
property. Also, make plans now for possible evacuations

A little ridge will bring dry conditions to the area on Thursday
with a weak likely inconsequential system still slated for 
Friday.

&&

.AVIATION...28/0400Z.

At 0400Z at KLAX, There was no marine layer. There was a surface-
based inversion. The top of the inversion was at 1300 feet with a
temp of 24 deg C.

High confidence in VFR TAFs.

KLAX...High confidence in TAF. Good confidence that any east wind
component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...27/737 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Expecting Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas with 
areas of SCA level winds to persist through tonight. Then conds 
will be largely below SCA levels Saturday through Monday before 
winds and seas increase Monday night to SCA levels ahead of an 
approaching strong storm system. Winds are expected to increase 
to SCA to Gale Force Tuesday and continue through Wednesday, along
with large and increasingly hazardous seas as the storm impacts 
the area. SCA winds and seas will continue Wednesday night, with 
a 50% chance of Gale Force winds.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Expecting SCA level winds and seas
to linger through late tonight. Conds will be largely below SCA 
levels Saturday through Monday evening before winds increase late 
Monday night to SCA levels ahead of an approaching strong storm 
system. Winds are expected to increase further to Gale Force 
Tuesday as the storm impacts the area. Winds and seas to SCA 
levels can be expected Tuesday night, with seas to SCA levels 
persisting Wednesday and Wednesday night.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate 
confidence in current forecast. Through Monday evening, winds and 
seas are expected to remain below SCA levels. Winds are expected 
to increase to SCA levels Monday night ahead of an approaching 
strong storm system. Gale Force winds are expected Tuesday and 
Tuesday night as the storm impacts the region. Winds to SCA levels
are expected for the southern waters Wednesday, otherwise conds 
should be below SCA levels Wednesday and Wednesday night.

It looks very likely that there will be significant impacts over 
the coastal waters from the Pacific storm system forecast mainly 
from Monday night into Wednesday. Gale Force winds and hazardous 
seas will spread to all the coastal waters with this system, along
with the potential for squalls with thunderstorms and waterspouts.
Poor visibility in heavy rain is also expected. Mariners are 
encouraged to pay close attention to the latest forecasts and any 
future statements regarding this storm system.

&&

.BEACHES...27/740 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will continue to slowly subside
across the waters. High surf will continue through Saturday 
across the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, as well 
as the Ventura and Los Angeles County coasts. There will be many,
strong rip nearly everywhere, strong long shore currents, some 
risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, and coastal erosion. 
These conditions will lead to an increased risk of drowning and 
make swimming dangerous.

In addition, an exceptionally high tide of up to 7.2 feet is 
predicted for Saturday morning, and this will continue the threat 
of minor to moderate coastal flooding over low-lying coastal 
areas. A Coastal Flood Advisory continues until 2 PM Saturday for 
the Ventura County beaches. Elsewhere, low-lying coastal areas 
with no protection from the ocean will still be vulnerable to sea
water intrusion during the Saturday morning high tide.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories in effect.
